content: Photo Credit: Paramount+ Curious to know why there’s no new episode of MobLand Season 2 on Paramount+ tonight? The current season follows a bitter power struggle that brews in the family as every member of it gets desperate to gain control of the North London empire. Harry, who remains stuck in this chaos, continues to deal with a corrupt detective, new cartels, and internal rivalries. Along the way, he must also ensure that he and his family remain safe. As a new episode aired last Friday, many are left wondering why there isn’t one this week. Why MobLand Season 2 isn’t airing a new episode this week MobLand Season 2 consisted of only 10 episodes and has officially concluded. Its finale, titled “The Queen is Dead,” premiered on November 20, 2026. However, fans need not worry, as another season is in store. On the same day as Season 2’s conclusion, it was announced that a third season is in production. In the final episode, coordinated raids put Harrigan’s empire at massive risk. Meanwhile, Harry makes a ruthless deal, with Conrad having approved it before. Maive raises the stakes, whereas Frankie takes a big risk. Moreover, Eddie backs down once again. The production update was also confirmed by Helen Mirren on the red carpet at the premiere of her new film A Talent for Murder. She said, “We’re starting work on a third season. We start next week.” At the time of writing, there’s no official news about what the storyline will be or when the season will be released. If the previous season’s pattern is considered, the series should ideally come out late next year. In an earlier conversation, MobLand’s executive producer David Glasser shared a cryptic update on what could happen in the upcoming season. title: David Fincher Brushes off AI Backlash Over Brad Pitt’s New Cliff Booth Movie
summary: David Fincher refuses to apologize for using AI in his latest Brad Pitt film. The director says critics have turned a technical choice into a culture war, and he insists the technology served the storytelling rather than replacing the people who make movies. David Fincher defends AI’s future in filmmaking Fincher pushed back against the […] The post David Fincher Brushes off AI Backlash Over Brad Pitt’s New Cliff Booth Movie appeared first on ComingSoon.net - Movie Trailers, TV & Streaming News, and More .
content: Photo Credit: Netflix David Fincher refuses to apologize for using AI in his latest Brad Pitt film. The director says critics have turned a technical choice into a culture war, and he insists the technology served the storytelling rather than replacing the people who make movies. David Fincher defends AI’s future in filmmaking Fincher pushed back against the uproar over The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth during an interview with El País 50 . Asked whether he anticipated the heated debate about AI reconstructing a version of Los Angeles and its television footage, he rejected the premise outright. “You know what the thing is? The debate over AI masks a culture war; it has nothing to do with movies,” he said. “I’ve never been in a situation where people cared about the tools I used.” The director framed his priority plainly: tell the story with the budget and schedule available. He noted that every production involves shooting a set number of sequences and animating them, and AI simply joined that toolkit. Fincher first confirmed the AI work on The Ringer ‘s Big Picture podcast, telling host Sean Fennessey that the technology synced a performer’s best vocal take with their best on-camera take when the two didn’t match. He estimated automated dialogue replacement covered just around 5% of the film, with the remainder handled through AI-assisted processes. Actors spent only four or five days re-recording dialogue above scenes. “We could use AI to re-lip that thing,” he said, describing the result as freeing. Fincher also outlined a future in which crews still handcraft sets and shoot masters repeatedly, while AI absorbs technical headaches like focus errors and hair drifting across a lens. “It’ll still be based on real human beings,” he said, adding that actors would repeat actions roughly 15 times instead of far more. Fennessey asked whether that prospect appealed to him. “Totally,” Fincher replied. Not everyone shares his enthusiasm. Early screenings of the Netflix film reportedly set off complaints about visible generative AI. Certain social media users have vowed to skip the Brad Pitt release altogether. Nonetheless, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is currently playing in select IMAX theaters, with a December 23 release set on Netflix. content: Photo Credit: @UniversalPictures / YouTube Christopher Nolan’s 2026 blockbuster The Odyssey brought Homer’s ancient epic to theaters with enormous scale and IMAX photography. Now available on 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray and digital platforms, the film raises a question: how should audiences experience it at home? Nolan has an answer. Christopher Nolan recommends using a projector to watch The Odyssey at home Nolan shared his home-viewing philosophy with Polygon, advocating for a setup that mimics the theatrical experience. He pointed to affordable projection technology as a way to elevate living-room screenings. This is the Christopher Nolan-approved way to watch movies at home. @odysseymovie pic.twitter.com/tV0AnS6Ken — Polygon (@Polygon) November 26, 2026 “I’m a big fan of projectors,” Nolan quipped. “You can get a relatively low-cost, pretty high-quality projector dock in your living room, maybe introduce some popcorn into the equation or whatever. You know, have a little mini movie theater.” The director also noted that home viewing enables a different kind of engagement. Audiences can pause, rewind, and study details at their own pace, things a cinema screening doesn’t allow. He added that The Odyssey retains an event-like quality even outside theaters, given its lengthy theatrical run. Universal released the film on November 17 with a 1.78:1 aspect ratio that fills a standard widescreen television. The theatrical IMAX version used a taller 1.43:1 ratio, so the home release trims a small amount of image from the top and bottom. The Odyssey follows Matt Damon’s Odysseus as he fights to return to Ithaca after the Trojan War, battling mythical creatures and dangerous gods along the way. The film’s massive scale and IMAX photography made premium theatrical screenings especially rewarding, and Nolan’s projector suggestion helps narrow the gap between cinema and the living room. Home viewing also lets audiences focus on quieter elements. Damon’s take on Odysseus explores loyalty, identity, and the aftermath of war. Robert Pattinson’s performance and the film’s treatment of Homer’s mythology reward closer attention when spectacle isn’t dominating the screen. The physical release bundles 12 behind-the-scenes featurettes covering the Trojan Horse construction, Moroccan battlefield sets, practical effects, stunts, and Ludwig Göransson’s score. content: Photo Credit: Lionsgate Mckenna Grace treated her role in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping like a mission. The actor, who plays Maysilee Donner and her twin sister Merrilee Donner, came on set with detailed notes and lobbied director Francis Lawrence to preserve small book-accurate touches. She now confirms which details survived the adaptation and why they mattered to her. How Mckenna Grace brought more of Maysilee Donner’s book personality to the screen Grace told PEOPLE that she showed up daily with a list of requests for Lawrence. “Every day I would show up to set with a list of things and thoughts and questions to bother Francis with,” Mckenna Grace quipped. “Yeah, I got the hummingbird, the Mockingjay pins in there. I got my braid.” Her persistence became a running joke among the cast. Whitney Peak, who plays Lenore Dove Baird, recalled Grace carrying a binder and declaring, “‘I need this and this and this and this and this.'” Grace also fought for a subtle costume choice tied to Maysilee’s identity in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping . She wanted different-colored eyeshadows to match each outfit, arguing that Maysilee would cling to her own style no matter what the Capitol imposed. “And so I wanted to find something that differentiated her outfit from just what the Capitol gave her,” Grace explained. Moreover, her push for fidelity grew from long-standing fandom . Grace read all the Hunger Games books while filming one of the Annabelle movies and watched the original films on set. She later questioned Josh Hutcherson about his experience, including whether his days were “as brutally physical as ours, which they were.” Peak credited Grace’s influence, saying Grace was in that writers’ room. Grace agreed that she was really tapped in. content: Photo Credit: Universal Pictures Tyrese Gibson , known for his role in Fast & Furious , has received heavy criticism on Instagram. The actor shared a video that appeared to make fun of domestic violence, sparking strong reactions from fans. Tyrese Gibson slammed over controversial Instagram video Earlier this week, Tyrese Gibson shared the video on Instagram where he appeared with fake cuts and bruises across his face. He also added a caption to the post which reads, “Domestic Violence is a problems [sic].” Gibson then explained that he had followed someone’s girlfriend on Instagram. He jokingly claimed that her boyfriend had beaten him up for doing so. The video showed him apologizing to the woman while washing the makeup off his face. The actor also joked about spending Thanksgiving by himself and said that his children spend the holidays with both parents. However, many people did not find the video funny. Several people questioned why he chose domestic violence for the joke. Many users also shared their reactions in the comments. One user wrote, “DV is a real problem. Nothing to joke about.” Another user, who survived domestic violence, commented, “Being a domestic violence survivor I don’t think this is funny at all.” A different user also expressed their disappointment with one user who simply wrote, “It’s not funny, Tyrese…” Another comment read, “Domestic violence isn’t funny. I don’t understand this video.” One user also directly addressed Gibson, writing, “I didn’t think it was funny, bro. With respect, you know what DV feels like; you’ve lived it. For a lot of women, that bruise isn’t makeup; it’s real. Man to man, survivor.” The backlash also comes in the context of past legal disputes and allegations involving the actor, all of which were previously addressed or resolved. Gibson faced abuse allegations from his pregnant girlfriend in 2007. According to CBS News police investigated the allegations, Gibson denied the claims, and no charges had been filed as of January 30, 2007. His first wife, Norma Mitchell, accused him of child abuse in 2017. Gibson denied the claims, calling them false and stating they damaged his career. Per E! News , authorities closed the child abuse investigation without filing criminal charges, and a judge denied Mitchell’s request for a permanent restraining order. In 2024, Mitchell also accused him of online harassment. Later that year, Gibson was taken into custody for contempt of court over unpaid child support to his second wife, Samantha Lee, for their daughter. As reported by PEOPLE , he was subsequently released after appealing the ruling. content: Photo Credit: Warner Bros. Pictures Robert Pattinson will play James Bond , and he already has support from one of cinema’s most respected filmmakers. The casting concludes months of speculation, with Amazon MGM and Denis Villeneuve confirming the star as Daniel Craig’s successor in the legendary 007 franchise. Luca Guadagnino is also interested in directing a Bond film Pattinson officially got the 007 part after a competitive search that reportedly included several British actors. From Jacob Elordi, Jack Lowden, and Callum Turner to Nicholas Hoult and Aaron Taylor-Johnson, the role was in contention before the studio settled on The Odyssey star. Now, Luca Guadagnino has endorsed Pattinson’s selection and shared his own ambitions regarding the franchise. Speaking to Variety at the Marrakech Film Festival, the Italian director called Pattinson “a perfect choice for James Bond.” Guadagnino said, “He’s an incredible star, he’s done so many great roles and I wish someday to work with him, of course.” When asked whether he would direct a Bond film himself, Guadagnino answered affirmatively. “I would say yes, yes, of course,” he stated. “I would like to play with icons.” The director also addressed rumors linking Pattinson to the iconic character Patrick Bateman, clarifying that the actor was never in contention for that part. The director, known for intimate character-driven films, mentioned he hopes his next project will be another love story, though he remains open to the world of James Bond. Robert Pattinson inherits the role after Craig’s five-movie run, which began with Casino Royale and ended with the character’s heroic sacrifice. The new era promises new creative energy, with Pattinson’s star power and Guadagnino’s public backing adding momentum to the franchise’s future. Steven Knight is writing the screenplay. Amy Pascal and David Heyman serve as producers, with Tanya Lapointe executive producing. The franchise now operates under Amazon MGM’s creative control following a major deal with longtime producers Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli. content: Photo Credit: Warner Bros. Pictures Sarah Michelle Gellar just revealed the one thing that keeps getting better in her 24-year marriage to Freddie Prinze Jr. The actress opened up about the secrets behind their lasting relationship while attending a red carpet event in Las Vegas . Sarah Michelle Gellar explains what makes her marriage to Freddie Prinze Jr. work While attending the PEOPLE x InStyle Drive-By Party 2026 in Las Vegas, Sarah Michelle Gellar recently opened up about her long-lasting marriage to Freddie Prinze Jr. The actress reflected on her relationship with Prinze Jr. and shared that their “communication” continues to get better over time. “I think that we’ve really learned how to be partners and support each other,” Gellar told PEOPLE . Gellar and Prinze Jr. first met while filming the 1997 movie I Know What You Did Last Summer. They got together in 2000 and later starred in the live-action Scooby-Doo movie in 2002. That same year, they tied the knot in Mexico after two years of dating. The couple shares daughter Charlotte Grace, 17, and son Rocky James, 14. The Buffy the Vampire Slayer alum marked their 24th anniversary by sharing throwback photos on Instagram. “@realfreddieprinze can you imagine telling these kids where they would be 24 years later (well tech 26… but 24 married),” she captioned the post. View this post on Instagram Gellar also told PEOPLE that keeping parts of their relationship private has strengthened their bond. “I always say I’m two people: I’m Sarah Michelle Gellar, and I’m Sarah Prinze. They’re different people,” she reflected. She also joked that having more than one bathroom has helped them avoid “a lot of petty fighting.” “You have to put the work in,” Gellar said. “And that goes for relationships, friendships, anything.” Prinze Jr. echoed similar sentiments in a July 2025 Variety interview. “I’m not perfect. She’s not perfect. We piss each other off, but we respect one another,” he said. “We were friends first. content: Photo Credit: Paramount Pictures Jack Black reunited with one of his youngest co-stars from School of Rock for a surprising musical collaboration over two decades later. The former child actor revealed why Black still stays connected to the film and its cast after all these years. Brian Falduto and Jack Black turn Billy’s famous insult from School of Rock into a country song Brian Falduto, who played Billy “Fancy Pants” in School of Rock (2003), has reunited with costar Jack Black on a new country EP. The actor-turned-country singer revealed the collaboration during an appearance on The Dory Jackson Interview series. Falduto’s upcoming EP, I Could Be Happy, features Black. The pair teamed up on “You’re Tacky & I Hate You (School of Rock Reunion),” a track inspired by Billy’s memorable catchphrase from the film. The song brought multiple former castmates back into the studio together. Falduto admitted he was reluctant at first to revisit the line but ultimately saw it as a chance to reconnect. “This idea of turning it into a reunion was really enriching for me because I was like, then I get to work with my friends again, and I get to see everybody, and we can make something really cool,” Falduto said. His former costars enthusiastically agreed to participate in the project. Falduto believes Black’s deep connection to the film keeps their bond strong after more than two decades. “I think the reason Jack still even gives us the time of day, never mind sings on my song, is because that was also a really special thing for him,” Falduto said. He added that School of Rock represented a career breakthrough for Black. “He got to do something he really loved, and that was comedic, and it tied to his music. I think it’s a very fond project for him,” Falduto explained. Black’s involvement in Falduto’s music career stretches back several years. The Tenacious D member previously helped produce the music video for Falduto’s 2020 song “God Loves Me Too.” Falduto also revealed the School of Rock cast still maintains an active group chat. “I don’t know of many major motion pictures where you can say that you still have an active group text 23 years later,” Falduto said. content: Photo Credit: CBS A longtime Emmy-winning CBS reporter announced their retirement on social media. Consequently, they are bringing an impressive 41-year journalism career to a close. The veteran journalist joined WCBS-TV in 2002, ending a dedicated two-decade run at the station. They started covering the northern suburbs before moving to the CBS Broadcast Center in Manhattan. Ultimately, they leave behind a lasting legacy in broadcast news. Tony Aiello announces retirement from CBS New York In his latest Facebook post, Aiello shared a compilation video of his broadcasting memories alongside a lengthy note. He expressed his gratitude for the opportunity as he announced that he’s stepping down as CBS reporter. “In September, 1985, a recent grad of Indiana University piled his stuff into a ’77 Buick and drove from Chicago to Virginia. He was taking a job at a radio station he’d never listened to, in a city he’d never visited. News reporter and fill-in DJ, Sunday to Friday, $200 a week,” he wrote. It was an inauspicious first step on my long and fulfilling career path.41 years later – 24 of them at CBS New York – I’m ready to sign off. I leave Channel 2 with a heart full of gratitude,” he added. He went on to thank management for believing in him and allowing him to work at an amazing place. Furthermore, the reporter expressed gratitude for the opportunity to travel, meet people, tell stories, and share in the network’s achievements. In addition, Aiello’s note continued with thanks to people including his colleagues, his family, the crew, senior management, people of the Tri-State, and reporters across NYC media, among others. “I’ve seen a lot of change in the news business over 41 years, and the change seems to be accelerating. The challenges are growing. To all of you who remain in the fight – stay strong. Stay focused on the mission to inform, enlighten, and serve, he stated. “And stay attentive to your own mental and physical well-being, because no job is worth compromising what really matters. I have toiled proudly in the vineyard of local news. Now I raise a glass of gratitude for the privilege. I am a lucky man,” he said, referring to the evolving nature of the profession. content: Photo Credit: Netflix The Hunting Wives Season 2 features another deadly thrill ride through Maple Brook, Texas, and not everyone survives. Episode 6 brings the season’s most shocking moment, and series creator Rebecca Perry Cutter explains why this tragedy had to happen. Rebecca Perry Cutter on the deadly consequences of The Hunting Wives Season 1 Margo comes home from church to find Brad in her living room. She saw him disrupt the service in a hospital gown, begging his father for help, but she missed what happened behind closed doors: Brad shot his father for answering a police call. The two sit down for a calm conversation, yet he soon turns suspicious. Brad starts doubting whether his mother really killed Abby, and when he recalls Margo mentioning an abortion, he accuses her of murder. They both lunge for the gun. Margo wins the race and kills Brad inside her own house. Sophie later backs Margo’s self-defense claim to police. Rebecca Perry Cutter told TVLine she wrote this downfall because George Ferrier “could do more than he did in Season 1,” and he proves it across these six episodes. The creator defends the death as essential storytelling. “I think it’s important that things have consequences,” she says. Brad, she notes, suffered more than anyone in Season 1: his girlfriend died, his mother died, and everyone blamed his mom for murder. Cutter wanted viewers to watch that pain play out rather than disappear. She adds that the character endures trauma, gets sent away by a father who cannot cope, and spirals into ruin. That arc, she says, was something the writers really wanted to explore. Darkness swallows Brad before the end. During an ayahuasca trip, he hallucinates his dead mother Jill, who angrily breastfeeds him and claims he will always belong to her. He bludgeons the vision to death. The Hunting Wives Season 2 episode is now streaming on Netflix. content: Photo Credit: NBC Mandy Noell took to social media to announce her departure from News 4 San Antonio. She reflected on her journey, highlighting the friendships she made along the way. Her announcement comes amid layoffs at the station and its sister station, KABB, which also saw the departures of personalities Chuck Miketinac and Alex Garcia. Mandy Noell is leaving News 4 San Antonio after three years Noell shared her picture at News 4 San Antonio alongside a lengthy note on Facebook . She announced her departure from the station on November 25, 2026. As she looked back on her journey, she acknowledged the many experiences she had shared with the team, from the highs to the lows. The anchor continued, “From reporting along our southern border to standing alongside communities experiencing unimaginable loss in the Hill Country, I’ve had the privilege of witnessing the remarkable generosity, compassion and resilience of the people who call South Texas home.” She further expressed her gratitude to the viewers for inviting her “into their lives on some of their very best days and some of their very worst. That is a responsibility I have never taken lightly.” Noell also spoke about the friendships she made on her time at the station, adding that “this community” made her journey “meaningful.” Her post further reads, “There is something truly special about San Antonio. I feel incredibly fortunate to have experienced it, not just as a journalist, but as a member of this community.” Noell said that on this Thanksgiving she has “so very much to be grateful for.” The journalist mentioned that she does have “a few newscasts” remaining, which she thoroughly wants to enjoy. Although Noell did not reveal her future career plans, she said she would share more details later. She concluded her note with a heartfelt thank-you to San Antonio.
